violated_contract: When an optimistic write fails, the client must put back the values that write replaced. Rebuilding them from the request instead (the opposite of the requested flag, a hard-coded null) shows a state the server never held. The web Tasks page reverted a failed completion toggle to completed: !completed, completed_at: null, so a completed task whose reopen failed came back completed but without its completion time, which the server still had: its row lost the completion date, it sank to the bottom of the Completed list, and the streak and exports no longer saw when it was done.
canonical_prevention: Capture the item before the optimistic write and, on failure, restore every field the write overwrote from that capture, as the hook's due-date and description handlers already do. Prove it with a hermetic test whose write rejects and which asserts each overwritten field is back to its value from before the write, not only the toggled flag.
